section: Georgia corporate income and franchise taxes
label: Corporate income tax rate
note: Flat rate on Georgia taxable net income. HB 463 (signed May 11, 2026) cut the rate from 5.19% to 4.99% beginning January 1, 2026, per the Governor's office.
source_title: Georgia Department of Revenue: Corporate Income and Net Worth Tax

section: Georgia corporate income and franchise taxes
label: Net worth tax: no tax due at or below this net worth
note: Corporations with a net worth of $100,000 or less owe no net worth tax but must still file a return.
source_title: Georgia Department of Revenue: Corporate Income and Net Worth Tax

section: Georgia corporate income and franchise taxes
label: Net worth tax: maximum annual tax
note: The maximum net worth tax applies to net worth over $22 million.
source_title: Georgia Department of Revenue: Corporate Income and Net Worth Tax

label: Levied by
value: County governing authorities, other local taxing jurisdictions and boards of education
note: Each taxing jurisdiction sets its own millage rate every year.
source_title: Georgia Department of Revenue: Filing Property Tax in Georgia

label: State oversight
value: Georgia Department of Revenue, Local Government Services
note: County boards of tax assessors value property; the Revenue Commissioner checks county digests for uniformity.
source_title: Georgia Department of Revenue: Local Government Services

label: Assessment ratio
note: Property is taxed on 40% of fair market value unless the law says otherwise (O.C.G.A. 48-5-7).
source_title: Georgia Department of Revenue: Property Tax Valuation

label: Statewide standard homestead exemption
note: Deducted from the 40% assessed value; applies to county and school taxes. Many counties grant larger local exemptions.
source_title: Georgia Department of Revenue: Property Tax Homestead Exemptions

label: Real estate transfer tax rate
value: $1.00 for the first $1,000 of sale price plus $0.10 per additional $100 (about $1.00 per $1,000)
note: Paid before the deed can be recorded with the clerk of the superior court (O.C.G.A. 48-6-1 to 48-6-10).
source_title: Georgia Department of Revenue: Real Estate Transfer Tax

label: Who pays the transfer tax
value: Seller (by law); the contract may shift it to the buyer
note: Taxes on the transfer of real estate. Each row has its own official source.
source_title: Georgia Department of Revenue: Real Estate Transfer Tax

label: Intangible recording tax on long-term mortgage notes
value: $1.50 per $500 of the note's face amount (maximum $25,000 per note)
note: Charged when the security instrument for a long-term note secured by Georgia real estate is recorded; the lender may pass it on to the borrower.
source_title: Georgia Department of Revenue: Intangible Recording Tax
